sentences.text: The prosecution contended that accused committed the offences punishable U/s.279 & 304(A) of IPC.

Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.

The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must C.C.No.586/2021 be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.

23. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide.
24.

In the instant case prosecution is relying on the version of eye witness and contended in the instant case prosecution examined 4 eye witnesses and all of them supported the case of the prosecution and hence they have proved their case.

Per contra the counsel for the accused contended that in the instant case the eye witness does not inspire confidence and all of them are planted witnesses and he relied on the cross-examination version of the eye witness and disputed the incident itself.
He contended his vehicle has not dashed to deceased vehicle as contended by the prosecution.
It is the deceased who came in negligent manner and dashed to moving bus on left portion and sustained injury, here the accident has taken place due to contributory negligence of the deceased.
25. The prosecution relied its case on P.W.1 to 5.

P.W.1 is the security and friend of deceased, PW2 is the C.C.No.586/2021 supervisor of deceased and pw6 is the inmate of the apartment all of them are known to deceased and they are interested witness

, pw1 and 2 claims no function but other 2 eye witness deposed that CM function was scheduled and hence they were deputed, Pw6 claims he was inside the compound and accident has taken place in front of gate, he claims people gathered there prior to accident for witnessing the function if that is true why no independent person is examined by the prosecution why they rely on apartment staff and resident, further they examine two police personnel one claims he was on the other side upon hearing sound he came there and other was at a a distance of 300 mtrs those did not see the accident live and they cannot depose on negligence,
here all the witness claims about existence of CCTV but the said footage is not produced before the court.

The other witness examined by the prosecution is investigating officer who deposed about duty.
26.
The burden is upon the prosecution to establish that the accused being the driver of bus drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

To bring home the culpability of accused under section 279 and 304(A) IPC, it is necessary to know the relevant provisions of law which reads as follows:
Section 279. Rash driving or riding on a public way:
Ks Layout Trps vs Kumar K M on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153482079/
7

Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to C.C.No.586/2021 be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
In the case on hand P.W.1 to 5 claims the accused drove his vehicle in high speed and caused accident.
Whether high speed alone constitutes negligence Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled "State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)"

entities.text: State of Karnataka Vs. Satish ((1998) 8 SCC 493)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: wherein the Apex Court observed: "merely because the truck was being driven at a high speed does not bespeak of either "negligence or rashness" by itself.

None of the witness examined by the prosecution could give any indication, even approximately,
as to what they meant by "high speed".
High speed is a relative term.
It was for the prosecution to bring on record material to establish as to what it meant by high speed in the facts and circumstances of the case.

In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions.
There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case.
In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the C.C.No.586/2021 maxim "res ipsa loquitur".
Mere fact that an innocent died in a road accident cannot be a reason to raise any presumption of rashness and negligence in absence of any other cogent evidence.
27. Prosecution contended accused drove his vehicle in high speed in negligent manner and dashed to bicycle which was coming from opposite road.
Upon perusal of the sketch map the accident has taken place in the center of the road.
Deceased was proceeding in same road which is 40ft road.
Those facts clearly shows accused was proceeding in main road.
It is normal presumption that a person entering main road from bicycle should be cautious and then enter the main road.
In the case on hand since the accident has taken place exactly in the junction the version of the eye witness that accused dashed to rear side of the bicycle appears doubtful.
As discussed earlier the bus sustained no damages
It cannot be brushed out completely that the deceased came in negligent manner dashed to proceeding bus in the main road.
The contention of the accused the deceased came al of a suudden and dashed to accused vehicle appears true.
Here prosecution has to establish the negligent act on the part of the accused.

With regard to negligent act the Hon'ble Apex court in "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs State of Andhra Pradesh reported in 2000 SCC(CRI) 1281, wherein the Court C.C.No.586/2021 discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:
"A rash act is primarily an over hasty act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is opposed to a deliberate act.
Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution.
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences.

Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution guarding against injury to the Ks Layout Trps vs Kumar K M on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153482079/
8 public generally or to any individual in particular.

entities.text: Ks Layout Trps vs Kumar K M on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution."
28. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.

Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show accused drove his vehicle in negligent manner, the burden is upon the prosecution to establish the same but they failed to establish same.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
29. Therefore, looking to the evidence available on record and the materials placed by way of oral and exhibits, the case of prosecution appears to be doubtful.
There is doubt as to whether the accused has driven his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of C.C.No.586/2021 the case, the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
Accordingly, the points under consideration are answered point No.1 and 2 IN THE NEGATIVE.

30. POINT No.3: In view of the above discussions and findings I proceed to pass the following ORDER Acting U/sec. 255(1) of Criminal procedure code, the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences alleged against him punishable U/sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
Bail bonds of accused and surety bonds shall stand canceled after completion of appeal period.

7. The point that arises for my determination is as under:

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Section 279 IPC deals with rash and negligent driving of any vehicle or riding on a public way in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
In order to constitute an offence U/s.279 of IPC, it must be established that the accused was driving the vehicle on a public way in rash and negligent manner to endanger human life or to likely cause to hurt or injury to any other person.
For the purpose of section 279 rash and negligent may be described as criminal rashness or criminal negligence.
It must be more than mere carelessness of error of judgment.
The essential ingredients of section 279 are: (1) rash and negligent driving or riding on a public way, (ii) The act must C.C.No.586/2021 be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person.
23. In order to constitute offence U/s.304(a) of IPC the prosecution must establish the essential ingredients of Sec.304(A) of IPC which are as follows: (I) The death of the person must be in question (ii) The death must have caused by the accused; and (iii) The act of the accused was rash or negligent and it did not amount to culpable homicide.
24.
In the instant case prosecution is relying on the version of eye witness and contended in the instant case prosecution examined 4 eye witnesses and all of them supported the case of the prosecution and hence they have proved their case.
The burden is upon the prosecution to establish that the accused being the driver of bus drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
It was for the prosecution to bring on record material to establish as to what it meant by high speed in the facts and circumstances of the case.
In a criminal trial, the burden of providing everything essential to the establishment of the charge against an accused always rests on the prosecution and there is a presumption of innocence in favour of the accused until the contrary is proved.
Criminality is not to be presumed subject of course to some statutory exceptions.
There is no statutory exception pleaded in the present case.
In the absence of any material on record, no presumption of rashness or negligence could be drawn by invoking the C.C.No.586/2021 maxim "res ipsa loquitur".
Mere fact that an innocent died in a road accident cannot be a reason to raise any presumption of rashness and negligence in absence of any other cogent evidence.
Upon perusal of the sketch map the accident has taken place in the center of the road.
Deceased was proceeding in same road which is 40ft road.
Those facts clearly shows accused was proceeding in main road.
It is normal presumption that a person entering main road from bicycle should be cautious and then enter the main road.
In the case on hand since the accident has taken place exactly in the junction the version of the eye witness that accused dashed to rear side of the bicycle appears doubtful.
As discussed earlier the bus sustained no damages
It cannot be brushed out completely that the deceased came in negligent manner dashed to proceeding bus in the main road.
It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution."
28. The witnesses have not stated rash and negligent act on the part of the accused on the date of alleged incident.
Further eye witnesses have not stated the rash and negligent act of the accused to show accused drove his vehicle in negligent manner, the burden is upon the prosecution to establish the same but they failed to establish same.
Therefore, in this circumstance of the case, the case of prosecution regarding rash and negligent act of accused could not be made out beyond reasonable doubt.
There is doubt as to whether the accused has driven his vehicle in a rash and negligent manner, so as to endanger the human life and personal safety of others.
Therefore, in the circumstances of C.C.No.586/2021 the case, the prosecution has failed to prove the alleged offence against the accused.
